newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London down, await Deng news.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London down, await Deng news.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London edged lower on Monday as the market looked for definitive news on the health of China's Paramount Leader Deng Xiaoping, traders said.
The Hang Seng reference index in London fell 71.84 points from Hong Kong's close, to 13,062.78 at 1454 GMT.

"The market is cautious and looking for news on Deng," one trader said, "If it is true (that Deng's health is failing) we'll see pressure on the index, but it's difficult to see how much it's been discounted."
The Hong Kong Hang Seng came off some 400 points last week on rumours the Deng may be ill, one trader said.
"We've had a strong FTSE and strong U.S. Treasury Bond, so Hong Kong would normally have been quite strong," he said, "But turnover was relatively low in Hong Kong."
Top officials of China's ruling Communist party returned to Beijing because the Paramount Leader's health was deteriorating, one source close to the party said.
Deng, 92, who retired from his last official post in 1990, has not been seen in public since 1994.
